news.headline: FTAI Aviation Ltd. Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026
Up to $1 billion in shares can now be bought back by FTAI Aviation
FTAI Aviation Maintains Outperform Rating, Price Target Lowered to $250
news.summary: On the eve of Q3 results, an analyst kept an Outperform rating on FTAI but cut the price target to $250, the latest in a string of target reductions after the stock's slide. Previews also highlight the FTAI Power segment, whose $1.465bn hyperscaler purchase order for 2027 Mod-1 deliveries is a key part of the bull case.

news.headline: KBRA and Fitch Assign Preliminary Ratings to FTAI's MRE 2026-2 Aircraft Lease-Backed Notes
news.summary: KBRA and Fitch assigned preliminary/expected ratings to MRE 2026-2, the second aircraft lease-backed securitization from FTAI's Strategic Capital platform after the $612M MRE 2026-1 deal in June. A repeat ABS issuance shows the asset-light SPV model can keep recycling capital through the debt markets.

news.headline: FTAI Aviation: Strong Growth, But The Valuation Doesn't Work
news.summary: A cautious Seeking Alpha analysis acknowledges FTAI's strong growth but argues the valuation still doesn't add up, a bearish counterpoint on the eve of Q3 results.

news.headline: FTAI Aviation stock hits 52-week low at $149.47
news.summary: FTAI shares hit a 52-week low of $149.47 intraday on October 23 and closed at about $154, days before Q3 results, after a 7-8% rebound on October 21 faded. The stock has lost roughly half its value from the $323 high amid aftermarket-sector selling and margin/power-business questions.

news.headline: Morgan Stanley Names Howmet Its Top Aerospace Pick, Replacing FTAI; Cuts FTAI Target to $310
news.summary: Morgan Stanley swapped FTAI out as its top commercial-aerospace pick in favour of Howmet, arguing the aftermarket selloff is overdone, and lowered its FTAI target to $310 from $360 while keeping an Overweight rating. The bank remains constructive on FTAI, but losing top-pick status removes a prominent sell-side tailwind ahead of Q3.

news.headline: Macquarie Initiates FTAI Aviation at Outperform With $305 Price Target
news.summary: Macquarie analyst Marni Lysaght launched coverage at Outperform with a $305 target, about 80% above the then-price of roughly $169, as part of a six-name aerospace initiation. The shares had fallen about a third over six months.

news.headline: FTAI Aviation Signs Multi-Year Engine Exchange Agreement With United Airlines, Extending the Program to CFM56-7B
news.summary: United expanded its maintenance, repair and exchange partnership with FTAI from the V2500 to CFM56-7B engines under a multi-year deal, receiving serviceable engines ahead of scheduled removals instead of shop visits. It is a marquee validation of FTAI's exchange model with a major U.S. carrier.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: Results due before market open today with an 8:00 a.m. ET call (announced October 6; the release was not yet retrievable from news sources or EDGAR at refresh time); consensus is roughly $1.43 EPS on about $1.0bn revenue. Key items: Aerospace Products EBITDA and margins, module/engine exchange volumes including the new United CFM56-7B program, FTAI Power commercial-launch timing (first Mod-1 deliveries now expected in 2027 against a $1.465bn hyperscaler order), SPV deployment and the MRE 2026-2 securitization, progress on the $500M buyback and whether the dividend is raised again.

catalysts.label: Investor meeting in New York
catalysts.detail: Scheduled investor meeting; a likely venue for 2027 guidance and an update on the asset-light SPV strategy.

pulse: FTAI rallied about 5% into the print to roughly $160-165 after hitting a 52-week low of $149.47 on October 23, still about half its $323 high, as the aerospace-aftermarket selloff, margin-reset worries and doubts about FTAI Power weigh on the shares; sell-side support persists (Macquarie Outperform/$305, Morgan Stanley Overweight/$310) but targets keep drifting lower, with a fresh cut to $250 at Outperform on October 28. The business keeps executing (United CFM56-7B exchange deal, second Strategic Capital ABS MRE 2026-2 rated by KBRA and Fitch). Q3 results due October 29 before the open (EPS consensus about $1.43, revenue about $1.0bn, ~50% growth) are the key test for margins, module volumes, the Power launch timeline and the buyback ahead of the December 10 investor meeting; the actual figures were not yet available at this refresh.
